cells.tense: You are walking by whatever light the next step gives you, and you have stopped asking for more.
cells.ask: Take the one next step tonight instead of planning the whole thing, and leave the plan unwritten — the act is the offer, not the fix.
cells.core:
You've stopped needing to see everything before you start. What you can see is what you use, and you move on it. Most people wait for more certainty than you've learned to do without, and it costs them the step.

A hunch or a dream arrives and you check it against what you've actually lived, and the two line up. You don't force meaning onto things. Afterward, you notice how it all fit, and you trust that noticing because it matches. The bend shows when someone presses you for the whole picture — you give them the next step, and it holds. One step, then the next, and the pattern shows itself from the walking.
cells.sheetLine: You walk by the light you have and stop asking for more.
cells.verb: moving through uncertainty without forcing clarity
cells.place: standing outside the system while still inside it

cells.tense: You are living in a version of this that hasn't happened yet, and the telling of it is pulling ahead of the life.
cells.ask: Let one thing you're carrying stay uninterpreted for a day — no meaning assigned, no ending written, nothing made into a sign.
cells.core:
You've been seeing the whole shape of something — a dream, a plan, a meaning — and treating it as already true. The vision runs ahead of what's actually happened, and you live inside it instead of beside it. Symbol and fact have gotten hard to tell apart, and you feel it when you catch yourself describing a future as though you'd already been there.

The quieter version: a dream lands and you let it stay a dream until life confirms it. In excess, everything means something immediately — a coincidence becomes a sign, a plan becomes a destiny — and the meaning crowds out the day you're in. The correction isn't to stop imagining. It's to hold what's growing without gripping it, to tend it without needing it finished.

cells.tense: You stopped trusting the dream a long time ago, and you've been standing at that door ever since.
cells.ask: Say one thing you actually want — plainly, no frame around it — and let it be small, unfinished, and not yet explained.
cells.core:
You've cut yourself off from the depths — you don't trust the hunch, you don't read the dream, you call all of it soft. So you're left with the flat version of things, and you defend it as being realistic. You know there's more to this than what you're admitting, and you've stopped letting yourself go near it.

The way back is quieter than you'd expect: you know what matters before you can say why, and that's enough. Not imagination — the willingness to attend to what arrives without proof. Direct knowing lands and you don't argue with it. That kind of knowing is quiet and accurate, and you've learned to distrust it. Let one perception land before you've justified it, and the rest starts to return.
cells.sheetLine: You've cut off the depths, and you call it being realistic.

cells.tense: You are already shaping what this becomes, and you talk about it as if it were happening on its own.
cells.ask: Keep one small practice for the next three days — same time, same seat, ten minutes — and say it's yours when you sit down.
cells.core:
You're the one finding meaning in this, giving it a shape, deciding where it heads — and you talk about it like it's just what the situation is. The dreaming keeps moving. Nobody has signed it.

This isn't passive. You set the direction; you just haven't owned that out loud, to yourself or anyone else. The practice is yours and steady — you sit with something and understand it a little better each time, patient rather than strained. Where it slips, the practice drifts; you do the work but don't own it, and the dreams shape you while you call them circumstances. One small, steady act of attention, named as yours, starts returning the pen.
cells.sheetLine: You're already dreaming this. You just haven't said so.

A reader could reasonably say their dreams are not integrated at all; the ask survives that because it is one watched act of the day, not a verdict on their life.
